ctd_blind_local_v3 — round 0 — the model as built

Build a model of this CTD phosphorylation time course that explains the measured distributions, and say what it implies about how P-TEFb modifies the substrate. Report explicitly what these data can and cannot establish about the mechanism. In particular, test whether the modification of a repeat changes the rate at which its immediate neighbours in the array are modified, against the alternatives that the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified (cooperativity between repeats) or on nothing at all, and say which of these the data can and cannot separate. Also test the earlier conclusion, drawn by eye, that the kinase acts distributively rather than processively.

CTD_0speciesCTD constructs (8 heptarepeats) with no repeat phosphorylated; maps to readout phos0_reluM; total over CTD_0..CTD_8 is 100 uMthe single configuration with no marks
CTD_1speciesCTD with exactly 1 of 8 repeats phosphorylated (Ser2 or Ser5, one bit per repeat); maps to phos1_reluMall 8 configurations with one mark
CTD_2speciesCTD with exactly 2 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos2_reluMall 28 configurations with two marks
CTD_3speciesCTD with exactly 3 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos3_reluMall 56 configurations with three marks
CTD_4speciesCTD with exactly 4 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos4_reluMall 70 configurations with four marks
CTD_5speciesCTD with exactly 5 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos5_reluMall 56 configurations with five marks
CTD_6speciesCTD with exactly 6 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos6_reluMall 28 configurations with six marks
CTD_7speciesCTD with exactly 7 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos7_reluMall 8 configurations with seven marks
CTD_8speciesCTD with all 8 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos8_reluMthe single fully marked configuration
ATPspeciesATP in the reaction buffer; one consumed per repeat modifieduM, 3000 at t = 0
ADPspeciesADP produced by phosphoryl transfer; not observed, kept for mass balanceuM, 0 at t = 0
PTEFbspeciesP-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1) kinase; catalytic modifier, never consumedrelative units fixed at 1; absolute concentration absorbed into kmodfree and substrate-bound kinase together (encounters are fast relative to sampling)
kmodparameterper-repeat modification rate per unit kinase at saturating ATP1/min; a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n)*cp^n*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)
cpparametercount-cooperativity switch: fold change of the per-repeat rate per mark already on the moleculeneutral value 1 (off in base); log-scale bounds 0.2 to 5
q_procparameterprocessivity switch: probability the kinase modifies another repeat before releasingneutral value 0 (strictly distributive in base); bounds 1e-4 to 0.99 when switched on
K_ATPparameterATP half-saturation constant of the kinaseuM, fixed at 50; ATP stays saturating
vialparameterreaction volume compartment1; species are concentrations in uM
Antimony source (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_6;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^7*CTD_7;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_3: CTD_1 + 3 ATP -> CTD_4 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_4: CTD_1 + 4 ATP -> CTD_5 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_5: CTD_1 + 5 ATP -> CTD_6 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_6: CTD_1 + 6 ATP -> CTD_7 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_7: CTD_1 + 7 ATP -> CTD_8 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^6*CTD_1;
  Jp2_2: CTD_2 + 2 ATP -> CTD_4 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_3: CTD_2 + 3 ATP -> CTD_5 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_4: CTD_2 + 4 ATP -> CTD_6 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_5: CTD_2 + 5 ATP -> CTD_7 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_6: CTD_2 + 6 ATP -> CTD_8 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^5*CTD_2;
  Jp3_2: CTD_3 + 2 ATP -> CTD_5 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_3: CTD_3 + 3 ATP -> CTD_6 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_4: CTD_3 + 4 ATP -> CTD_7 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_5: CTD_3 + 5 ATP -> CTD_8 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^4*CTD_3;
  Jp4_2: CTD_4 + 2 ATP -> CTD_6 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_3: CTD_4 + 3 ATP -> CTD_7 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_4: CTD_4 + 4 ATP -> CTD_8 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^3*CTD_4;
  Jp5_2: CTD_5 + 2 ATP -> CTD_7 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  Jp5_3: CTD_5 + 3 ATP -> CTD_8 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc^2*CTD_5;
  Jp6_2: CTD_6 + 2 ATP -> CTD_8 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*q_proc*CTD_6;
end

PTEFbspeciesP-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1) kinase; catalytic modifier, never consumedrelative units fixed at 1; absolute concentration absorbed into kmodfree and substrate-bound kinase together (encounters are fast relative to sampling)
kmodparameterper-repeat modification rate per unit kinase at saturating ATP1/min; a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n)*cp^n*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)
cpparametercount-cooperativity switch: fold change of the per-repeat rate per mark already on the moleculeneutral value 1 (off in base); log-scale bounds 0.2 to 5
q_procparameterprocessivity switch: probability the kinase modifies another repeat before releasingneutral value 0 (strictly distributive in base); bounds 1e-4 to 0.99 when switched on
K_ATPparameterATP half-saturation constant of the kinaseuM, fixed at 50; ATP stays saturating
vialparameterreaction volume compartment1; species are concentrations in uM
Antimony source (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1.0; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_6;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^7*CTD_7;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_3: CTD_1 + 3 ATP -> CTD_4 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_4: CTD_1 + 4 ATP -> CTD_5 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_5: CTD_1 + 5 ATP -> CTD_6 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_6: CTD_1 + 6 ATP -> CTD_7 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_7: CTD_1 + 7 ATP -> CTD_8 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^6*CTD_1;
  Jp2_2: CTD_2 + 2 ATP -> CTD_4 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_3: CTD_2 + 3 ATP -> CTD_5 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;

  Jp4_2: CTD_4 + 2 ATP -> CTD_6 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;

kmodparameterper-repeat modification rate per unit kinase at saturating ATP1/min; a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n)*cp^n*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)
cpparametercount-cooperativity switch: fold change of the per-repeat rate per mark already on the moleculeneutral value 1 (off in base); log-scale bounds 0.2 to 5
q_procparameterprocessivity switch: probability the kinase modifies another repeat before releasingneutral value 0 (strictly distributive in base); bounds 1e-4 to 0.99 when switched on
K_ATPparameterATP half-saturation constant of the kinaseuM, fixed at 50; ATP stays saturating
vialparameterreaction volume compartment1; species are concentrations in uM
nbparameternearest-neighbour switch: fold change of an unmodified repeat's rate per phosphorylated immediate neighbour (m = 0, 1 or 2; repeats 1 and 8 have one neighbour)neutral value 1 (no neighbour effect); < 1 inhibition, > 1 facilitation; log10 scale, bounds 0.01 to 100
Antimony source (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; 0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; 0;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; 0;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; 0;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; 0;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; 0;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; 0;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; 0;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_3: CTD_1 + 3 ATP -> CTD_4 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_4: CTD_1 + 4 ATP -> CTD_5 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_5: CTD_1 + 5 ATP -> CTD_6 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_6: CTD_1 + 6 ATP -> CTD_7 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_7: CTD_1 + 7 ATP -> CTD_8 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^6*CTD_1;
  Jp2_2: CTD_2 + 2 ATP -> CTD_4 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_3: CTD_2 + 3 ATP -> CTD_5 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_4: CTD_2 + 4 ATP -> CTD_6 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_5: CTD_2 + 5 ATP -> CTD_7 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_6: CTD_2 + 6 ATP -> CTD_8 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^5*CTD_2;
  Jp3_2: CTD_3 + 2 ATP -> CTD_5 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_3: CTD_3 + 3 ATP -> CTD_6 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_4: CTD_3 + 4 ATP -> CTD_7 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_5: CTD_3 + 5 ATP -> CTD_8 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^4*CTD_3;
  Jp4_2: CTD_4 + 2 ATP -> CTD_6 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_3: CTD_4 + 3 ATP -> CTD_7 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_4: CTD_4 + 4 ATP -> CTD_8 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^3*CTD_4;
  Jp5_2: CTD_5 + 2 ATP -> CTD_7 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  Jp5_3: CTD_5 + 3 ATP -> CTD_8 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc^2*CTD_5;
  Jp6_2: CTD_6 + 2 ATP -> CTD_8 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*q_proc*CTD_6;
  // Positional refinement by gap class: Gf8 = unmodified; G<a><b>_<g...> = unmarked end stretches a <= b and unmarked interior stretches g... between marks; n = 8 - a - b - sum(g)
// Each G reaction from a class with n marks also carries CTD_n + ATP -> CTD_n+1 + ADP, so the G classes with n marks sum to CTD_n identically and ATP is consumed once per modification; J0-J7 are kept at zero rate
species Gf8 in vial, G07 in vial, G16 in vial, G25 in vial, G34 in vial;
species G06 in vial, G15 in vial, G24 in vial, G33 in vial, G05_1 in vial, G14_1 in vial, G23_1 in vial, G04_2 in vial;
species G13_2 in vial, G22_2 in vial, G03_3 in vial, G12_3 in vial, G02_4 in vial, G11_4 in vial, G01_5 in vial, G00_6 in vial;
species G05 in vial, G14 in vial, G23 in vial, G04_1 in vial, G13_1 in vial, G22_1 in vial, G03_2 in vial, G12_2 in vial, G02_3 in vial, G11_3 in vial;
species G01_4 in vial, G00_5 in vial, G03_11 in vial, G12_11 in vial, G02_21 in vial, G11_21 in vial, G01_31 in vial, G01_22 in vial, G00_41 in vial, G00_32 in vial;
species G04 in vial, G13 in vial, G22 in vial, G03_1 in vial, G12_1 in vial, G02_2 in vial, G11_2 in vial, G01_3 in vial;
species G00_4 in vial, G02_11 in vial, G11_11 in vial, G01_21 in vial, G00_31 in vial, G00_22 in vial, G01_111 in vial, G00_211 in vial;
species G03 in vial, G12 in vial, G02_1 in vial, G11_1 in vial, G01_2 in vial, G00_3 in vial, G01_11 in vial, G00_21 in vial, G00_111 in vial;
species G02 in vial, G11 in vial, G01_1 in vial, G00_2 in vial, G00_11 in vial, G01 in vial, G00_1 in vial, G00 in vial;

What the model means (entity glossary)

idkinddenotes / roleunit or conventionlumps / from axis
CTD_0speciesCTD constructs (8 heptarepeats) with no repeat phosphorylated; maps to readout phos0_reluM; total over CTD_0..CTD_8 is 100 uMthe single configuration with no marks
CTD_1speciesCTD with exactly 1 of 8 repeats phosphorylated (Ser2 or Ser5, one bit per repeat); maps to phos1_reluMall 8 configurations with one mark
CTD_2speciesCTD with exactly 2 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos2_reluMall 28 configurations with two marks
CTD_3speciesCTD with exactly 3 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos3_reluMall 56 configurations with three marks
CTD_4speciesCTD with exactly 4 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos4_reluMall 70 configurations with four marks
CTD_5speciesCTD with exactly 5 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos5_reluMall 56 configurations with five marks
CTD_6speciesCTD with exactly 6 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos6_reluMall 28 configurations with six marks
CTD_7speciesCTD with exactly 7 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos7_reluMall 8 configurations with seven marks
CTD_8speciesCTD with all 8 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos8_reluMthe single fully marked configuration
ATPspeciesATP in the reaction buffer; one consumed per repeat modifieduM, 3000 at t = 0
ADPspeciesADP produced by phosphoryl transfer; not observed, kept for mass balanceuM, 0 at t = 0
PTEFbspeciesP-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1) kinase; catalytic modifier, never consumedrelative units fixed at 1; absolute concentration absorbed into kmodfree and substrate-bound kinase together (encounters are fast relative to sampling)
kmodparameterper-repeat modification rate per unit kinase at saturating ATP1/min; a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n)*cp^n*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)
cpparametercount-cooperativity switch: fold change of the per-repeat rate per mark already on the moleculeneutral value 1 (off in base); log-scale bounds 0.2 to 5
q_procparameterprocessivity switch: probability the kinase modifies another repeat before releasingneutral value 0 (strictly distributive in base); bounds 1e-4 to 0.99 when switched on
K_ATPparameterATP half-saturation constant of the kinaseuM, fixed at 50; ATP stays saturating
vialparameterreaction volume compartment1; species are concentrations in uM
Antimony source (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1; q_proc = 0.1; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_6;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^7*CTD_7;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_3: CTD_1 + 3 ATP -> CTD_4 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_4: CTD_1 + 4 ATP -> CTD_5 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_5: CTD_1 + 5 ATP -> CTD_6 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_6: CTD_1 + 6 ATP -> CTD_7 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_7: CTD_1 + 7 ATP -> CTD_8 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^6*CTD_1;
  Jp2_2: CTD_2 + 2 ATP -> CTD_4 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_3: CTD_2 + 3 ATP -> CTD_5 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_4: CTD_2 + 4 ATP -> CTD_6 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_5: CTD_2 + 5 ATP -> CTD_7 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_6: CTD_2 + 6 ATP -> CTD_8 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^5*CTD_2;
  Jp3_2: CTD_3 + 2 ATP -> CTD_5 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_3: CTD_3 + 3 ATP -> CTD_6 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_4: CTD_3 + 4 ATP -> CTD_7 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_5: CTD_3 + 5 ATP -> CTD_8 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^4*CTD_3;
  Jp4_2: CTD_4 + 2 ATP -> CTD_6 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_3: CTD_4 + 3 ATP -> CTD_7 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_4: CTD_4 + 4 ATP -> CTD_8 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^3*CTD_4;
  Jp5_2: CTD_5 + 2 ATP -> CTD_7 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  Jp5_3: CTD_5 + 3 ATP -> CTD_8 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc^2*CTD_5;
  Jp6_2: CTD_6 + 2 ATP -> CTD_8 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*q_proc*CTD_6;
end

idkinddenotes / roleunit or conventionlumps / from axis
CTD_0speciesCTD constructs (8 heptarepeats) with no repeat phosphorylated; maps to readout phos0_reluM; total over CTD_0..CTD_8 is 100 uMthe single configuration with no marks
CTD_1speciesCTD with exactly 1 of 8 repeats phosphorylated (Ser2 or Ser5, one bit per repeat); maps to phos1_reluMall 8 configurations with one mark
CTD_2speciesCTD with exactly 2 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos2_reluMall 28 configurations with two marks
CTD_3speciesCTD with exactly 3 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos3_reluMall 56 configurations with three marks
CTD_4speciesCTD with exactly 4 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos4_reluMall 70 configurations with four marks
CTD_5speciesCTD with exactly 5 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos5_reluMall 56 configurations with five marks
CTD_6speciesCTD with exactly 6 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos6_reluMall 28 configurations with six marks
CTD_7speciesCTD with exactly 7 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos7_reluMall 8 configurations with seven marks
CTD_8speciesCTD with all 8 repeats phosphorylated; maps to phos8_reluMthe single fully marked configuration
ATPspeciesATP in the reaction buffer; one consumed per repeat modifieduM, 3000 at t = 0
ADPspeciesADP produced by phosphoryl transfer; not observed, kept for mass balanceuM, 0 at t = 0
PTEFbspeciesP-TEFb (CDK9/cyclin T1) kinase; catalytic modifier, never consumedrelative units fixed at 1; absolute concentration absorbed into kmodfree and substrate-bound kinase together (encounters are fast relative to sampling)

G00_3species5 marks; end gaps 0,0; interior gap 3; refines CTD_5uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_5end gaps {0,0}; interior {3}
G01_11species5 marks; end gaps 0,1; interior gaps 1,1; refines CTD_5uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_5end gaps {0,1}; interior {1,1}
G00_21species5 marks; end gaps 0,0; interior gaps 2,1; refines CTD_5uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_5end gaps {0,0}; interior {2,1}
G00_111species5 marks; end gaps 0,0; interior gaps 1,1,1; refines CTD_5uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_5end gaps {0,0}; interior {1,1,1}
G02species6 marks; end gaps 0,2; no interior gap; refines CTD_6uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_6end gaps {0,2}; interior {}
G11species6 marks, on repeats 2 to 7 (end gaps 1,1); refines CTD_6uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_6end gaps {1,1}; interior {}
G01_1species6 marks; end gaps 0,1; interior gap 1; refines CTD_6uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_6end gaps {0,1}; interior {1}
G00_2species6 marks; end gaps 0,0; interior gap 2; refines CTD_6uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_6end gaps {0,0}; interior {2}
G00_11species6 marks; end gaps 0,0; interior gaps 1,1; refines CTD_6uM; sums with its class-mates to CTD_6end gaps {0,0}; interior {1,1}
G01species7 marks, the unmarked repeat at an end (repeat 1 or 8); refines CTD_7uM; sums with G00_1 to CTD_7end gaps {0,1}; interior {}
G00_1species7 marks, the unmarked repeat interior (repeats 2 to 7); refines CTD_7uM; sums with G01 to CTD_7end gaps {0,0}; interior {1}
G00speciesall 8 repeats marked (equals CTD_8)uMthe single fully marked configuration
kmodparameterper-repeat modification rate per unit kinase at saturating ATP1/min; a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n)*cp^n*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)
cpparametercount-cooperativity switch: fold change of the per-repeat rate per mark already on the moleculeneutral value 1 (off in base); log-scale bounds 0.2 to 5
q_procparameterprocessivity switch: probability the kinase modifies another repeat before releasingneutral value 0 (strictly distributive in base); bounds 1e-4 to 0.99 when switched on
K_ATPparameterATP half-saturation constant of the kinaseuM, fixed at 50; ATP stays saturating
vialparameterreaction volume compartment1; species are concentrations in uM
nbparameternearest-neighbour switch: fold change of an unmodified repeat's rate per phosphorylated immediate neighbour (m = 0, 1 or 2; repeats 1 and 8 have one neighbour)neutral value 1 (no neighbour effect); < 1 inhibition, > 1 facilitation; log10 scale, bounds 0.01 to 100
Antimony source (model/antimony)
model ctd_ptefb_counts
  // CTD_n: CTD molecules with n of 8 repeats phosphorylated (one bit per repeat)
  compartment vial = 1;
  species CTD_0 in vial, CTD_1 in vial, CTD_2 in vial, CTD_3 in vial, CTD_4 in vial;
  species CTD_5 in vial, CTD_6 in vial, CTD_7 in vial, CTD_8 in vial;
  species ATP in vial, ADP in vial, PTEFb in vial;
  CTD_0 = 100; CTD_1 = 0; CTD_2 = 0; CTD_3 = 0; CTD_4 = 0;
  CTD_5 = 0; CTD_6 = 0; CTD_7 = 0; CTD_8 = 0;
  ATP = 3000; ADP = 0; PTEFb = 1;
  kmod = 0.01; cp = 1.0; q_proc = 0; K_ATP = 50;
  // single-repeat encounters: one modification per binding event (distributive)
  J0: CTD_0 + ATP -> CTD_1 + ADP; 0;
  J1: CTD_1 + ATP -> CTD_2 + ADP; 0;
  J2: CTD_2 + ATP -> CTD_3 + ADP; 0;
  J3: CTD_3 + ATP -> CTD_4 + ADP; 0;
  J4: CTD_4 + ATP -> CTD_5 + ADP; 0;
  J5: CTD_5 + ATP -> CTD_6 + ADP; 0;
  J6: CTD_6 + ATP -> CTD_7 + ADP; 0;
  J7: CTD_7 + ATP -> CTD_8 + ADP; 0;
  // processive encounters: j repeats per binding event, continuation probability q_proc (0 in base)
  Jp0_2: CTD_0 + 2 ATP -> CTD_2 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_3: CTD_0 + 3 ATP -> CTD_3 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_4: CTD_0 + 4 ATP -> CTD_4 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_5: CTD_0 + 5 ATP -> CTD_5 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_6: CTD_0 + 6 ATP -> CTD_6 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_7: CTD_0 + 7 ATP -> CTD_7 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^6*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_0;
  Jp0_8: CTD_0 + 8 ATP -> CTD_8 + 8 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*8*q_proc^7*CTD_0;
  Jp1_2: CTD_1 + 2 ATP -> CTD_3 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_3: CTD_1 + 3 ATP -> CTD_4 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_4: CTD_1 + 4 ATP -> CTD_5 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_5: CTD_1 + 5 ATP -> CTD_6 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_6: CTD_1 + 6 ATP -> CTD_7 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^5*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_1;
  Jp1_7: CTD_1 + 7 ATP -> CTD_8 + 7 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*7*cp*q_proc^6*CTD_1;
  Jp2_2: CTD_2 + 2 ATP -> CTD_4 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_3: CTD_2 + 3 ATP -> CTD_5 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_4: CTD_2 + 4 ATP -> CTD_6 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_5: CTD_2 + 5 ATP -> CTD_7 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^4*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_2;
  Jp2_6: CTD_2 + 6 ATP -> CTD_8 + 6 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*6*cp^2*q_proc^5*CTD_2;
  Jp3_2: CTD_3 + 2 ATP -> CTD_5 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_3: CTD_3 + 3 ATP -> CTD_6 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_4: CTD_3 + 4 ATP -> CTD_7 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^3*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_3;
  Jp3_5: CTD_3 + 5 ATP -> CTD_8 + 5 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*5*cp^3*q_proc^4*CTD_3;
  Jp4_2: CTD_4 + 2 ATP -> CTD_6 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_3: CTD_4 + 3 ATP -> CTD_7 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^2*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_4;
  Jp4_4: CTD_4 + 4 ATP -> CTD_8 + 4 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*4*cp^4*q_proc^3*CTD_4;
  Jp5_2: CTD_5 + 2 ATP -> CTD_7 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc*(1 - q_proc)*CTD_5;
  Jp5_3: CTD_5 + 3 ATP -> CTD_8 + 3 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*3*cp^5*q_proc^2*CTD_5;
  Jp6_2: CTD_6 + 2 ATP -> CTD_8 + 2 ADP; vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*2*cp^6*q_proc*CTD_6;
  // Positional refinement by gap class: Gf8 = unmodified; G<a><b>_<g...> = unmarked end stretches a <= b and unmarked interior stretches g... between marks; n = 8 - a - b - sum(g)
// Each G reaction from a class with n marks also carries CTD_n + ATP -> CTD_n+1 + ADP, so the G classes with n marks sum to CTD_n identically and ATP is consumed once per modification; J0-J7 are kept at zero rate
species Gf8 in vial, G07 in vial, G16 in vial, G25 in vial, G34 in vial;
species G06 in vial, G15 in vial, G24 in vial, G33 in vial, G05_1 in vial, G14_1 in vial, G23_1 in vial, G04_2 in vial;
species G13_2 in vial, G22_2 in vial, G03_3 in vial, G12_3 in vial, G02_4 in vial, G11_4 in vial, G01_5 in vial, G00_6 in vial;
species G05 in vial, G14 in vial, G23 in vial, G04_1 in vial, G13_1 in vial, G22_1 in vial, G03_2 in vial, G12_2 in vial, G02_3 in vial, G11_3 in vial;
species G01_4 in vial, G00_5 in vial, G03_11 in vial, G12_11 in vial, G02_21 in vial, G11_21 in vial, G01_31 in vial, G01_22 in vial, G00_41 in vial, G00_32 in vial;
species G04 in vial, G13 in vial, G22 in vial, G03_1 in vial, G12_1 in vial, G02_2 in vial, G11_2 in vial, G01_3 in vial;
species G00_4 in vial, G02_11 in vial, G11_11 in vial, G01_21 in vial, G00_31 in vial, G00_22 in vial, G01_111 in vial, G00_211 in vial;
species G03 in vial, G12 in vial, G02_1 in vial, G11_1 in vial, G01_2 in vial, G00_3 in vial, G01_11 in vial, G00_21 in vial, G00_111 in vial;
species G02 in vial, G11 in vial, G01_1 in vial, G00_2 in vial, G00_11 in vial, G01 in vial, G00_1 in vial, G00 in vial;

For every rate rule this base can switch on (independent repeats, count cooperativity cp^n, processive continuation that picks among the remaining unmodified repeats), all unmodified repeats of a …
full rationale
For every rate rule this base can switch on (independent repeats, count cooperativity cp^n, processive continuation that picks among the remaining unmodified repeats), all unmodified repeats of a molecule with n marks share one rate, so the 256 configurations are strongly lumpable by n and these 9 states reproduce the positional model's count distribution exactly. The 'nothing at all', 'cooperativity' and 'distributive vs processive' hypotheses therefore lose nothing by being counted. A nearest-neighbour effect is the one hypothesis that breaks the lumping, so it cannot be a switch on this base. Two previous replies to this brief failed the contract outright; a 1024-reaction hand enumeration, together with its 256-entry glossary and network, is not something this reply can carry reliably or check without execution. The next decision gives the exact rule so the positional model can be generated mechanically. A generator check comes free: at nb = 1 it must reproduce this base trajectory for trajectory.

no source givenmedium
Exact construction rule for the positional (neighbour) candidate, to be generated and not hand-written. Species C_b1b2b3b4b5b6b7b8 (b_i = 1 if repeat i, numbered from the N-terminus, is phosphorylated), C_00000000 = 100 uM, all others 0. For every configuration and every unmodified repeat i, one reaction to the configuration with b_i = 1, consuming one ATP and producing one ADP. Rate: vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^n*nb^m*C, where n = marks on the molecule and m = marked immediate neighbours of i (0 to 2; repeats 1 and 8 have one neighbour). New parameter nb, a fold change per marked neighbour: nominal and neutral value 1, bounds 0.01 to 100.
This is the minimal positional extension that separates 'a mark changes its neighbours' rate' (nb) from 'the rate depends on how many marks the molecule carries' (cp) and from neither (nb = cp = 1). …
full rationale
This is the minimal positional extension that separates 'a mark changes its neighbours' rate' (nb) from 'the rate depends on how many marks the molecule carries' (cp) and from neither (nb = cp = 1). It is 8*2^7 = 1024 reactions. Summing C over the C(8,n) configurations with n marks gives CTD_n, so readouts map onto it exactly as onto this base. nb < 1 (neighbour inhibition) jams molecules near 3 to 4 non-adjacent marks before slow filling, and that stall at intermediate counts between 2 h and 16 h is something cp alone cannot shape. nb > 1 gives nucleation-and-growth (bimodal 0-versus-high counts at 1 to 2 h), which cp > 1 and processivity also give. That is the likely indistinguishable set.

all alternatives considered
A directional neighbour effect (separate factors for N- and C-side neighbours) was not chosen: counts carry no positional information to separate the two directions, so it would add a flat direction. Pairwise or longer-range interactions were not chosen either: they are not the hypothesis named.
fittedmedium
Distributive single-repeat steps J0..J7. Each unmodified repeat is modified at kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP), mass action in the substrate at constant enzyme, so a molecule with n marks advances at (8 - n) times that rate. The template is phosphorylation X -> X_p with the kinase as modifier. Irreversible: no reverse step and no phosphatase.
The assay is purified kinase, CTD and ATP with no phosphatase, so removal of phosphate is not modelled. The kinase is catalytic and constant, so its level enters as a fixed multiplier. …
full rationale
The assay is purified kinase, CTD and ATP with no phosphatase, so removal of phosphate is not modelled. The kinase is catalytic and constant, so its level enters as a fixed multiplier. Mass action in CTD assumes the kinase is far from saturated by substrate. Neither the enzyme concentration nor a CTD Km is given, so saturation cannot be decided from the note. If all unmodified repeats bind alike, saturation would only reparameterise time by a factor common to every reaction (the same sequence of distributions, a different clock). With three post-zero time points that clock change is largely absorbed by kmod and cp, so it is named unresolved rather than built in. With cp = 1 and q_proc = 0 the count distribution is binomial(8, 1 - exp(-r*t)): the independent-repeat ('nothing at all') hypothesis.

Count-cooperativity switch cp: the per-repeat rate of a molecule carrying n marks is multiplied by cp^n. cp = 1 (base) turns it off; cp > 1 is positive and cp < 1 negative cooperativity between repeats.
One parameter expresses 'the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified' as a constant fold change per existing mark, the additive free-energy form. …
full rationale
One parameter expresses 'the rate depends only on how many repeats are already modified' as a constant fold change per existing mark, the additive free-energy form. It is the most parsimonious count-dependent law the data can constrain with 9 peaks at 3 informative time points. A free factor per n (7 parameters) would not be identifiable. Bounds 0.2 to 5 are 1.4 decades on cp but compound to ~10 decades on the n = 7 step. Wider bounds put the solver in stiff corners without adding plausible behaviour.
lab_note ['the rate depending only on how many repeats of the molecule are already modified (cooperativity between repeats, which was also raised as a possibility to look at)'] — count-dependent rate is one of the hypotheses to test
alternatives: A free rate per count n (unidentifiable). A saturating dependence on n (an extra shape parameter the data cannot see).
fittedmedium
Processivity switch q_proc on reactions Jp<n>_<j>. A binding event on a molecule with n marks starts at the same encounter rate as a distributive step. After each modification the kinase continues to another unmodified repeat with probability q_proc, else releases. The run is truncated only by running out of unmodified repeats (weights q^(j-1)(1-q), and q^(j-1) for the run that completes the molecule). q_proc = 0 (base) is strictly distributive.
Distributive versus processive is about how many modifications one binding event makes. …
full rationale
Distributive versus processive is about how many modifications one binding event makes. The encounter-level jump n -> n+j with geometric run length is the standard count-level representation, and its weights sum to 1, so q_proc changes what an encounter does, not how often encounters happen. Strong processivity predicts early bimodality (CTD_0 plus high counts, depleted intermediates at 1 h). Its difference from cp > 1 is memory: under processivity a released molecule returns to the slow distributive pace, so long-lived intermediates persist to the 16 h point. Sliding processivity (running along to the next repeat, stopped by an already-modified repeat) depends on positions and only exists in the positional model. It is not exactly lumpable and is likely aliased with nb > 1.

full rationale
For every rate rule this base can switch on (independent repeats, count cooperativity cp^n, processive continuation that picks among the remaining unmodified repeats), all unmodified repeats of a molecule with n marks share one rate, so the 256 configurations are strongly lumpable by n and these 9 states reproduce the positional model's count distribution exactly. The 'nothing at all', 'cooperativity' and 'distributive vs processive' hypotheses therefore lose nothing by being counted. A nearest-neighbour effect is the one hypothesis that breaks the lumping, so it cannot be a switch on this base. Two previous replies to this brief failed the contract outright; a 1024-reaction hand enumeration, together with its 256-entry glossary and network, is not something this reply can carry reliably or check without execution. The next decision gives the exact rule so the positional model can be generated mechanically. A generator check comes free: at nb = 1 it must reproduce this base trajectory for trajectory.

Exact construction rule for the positional (neighbour) candidate, to be generated and not hand-written. Species C_b1b2b3b4b5b6b7b8 (b_i = 1 if repeat i, numbered from the N-terminus, is phosphorylated), C_00000000 = 100 uM, all others 0. For every configuration and every unmodified repeat i, one reaction to the configuration with b_i = 1, consuming one ATP and producing one ADP. Rate: vial*kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^n*nb^m*C, where n = marks on the molecule and m = marked immediate neighbours of i (0 to 2; repeats 1 and 8 have one neighbour). New parameter nb, a fold change per marked neighbour: nominal and neutral value 1, bounds 0.01 to 100.
This is the minimal positional extension that separates 'a mark changes its neighbours' rate' (nb) from 'the rate depends on how many marks the molecule carries' (cp) and from neither (nb = cp = 1). …
full rationale
This is the minimal positional extension that separates 'a mark changes its neighbours' rate' (nb) from 'the rate depends on how many marks the molecule carries' (cp) and from neither (nb = cp = 1). It is 8*2^7 = 1024 reactions. Summing C over the C(8,n) configurations with n marks gives CTD_n, so readouts map onto it exactly as onto this base. nb < 1 (neighbour inhibition) jams molecules near 3 to 4 non-adjacent marks before slow filling, and that stall at intermediate counts between 2 h and 16 h is something cp alone cannot shape. nb > 1 gives nucleation-and-growth (bimodal 0-versus-high counts at 1 to 2 h), which cp > 1 and processivity also give. That is the likely indistinguishable set.

full rationale
The assay is purified kinase, CTD and ATP with no phosphatase, so removal of phosphate is not modelled. The kinase is catalytic and constant, so its level enters as a fixed multiplier. Mass action in CTD assumes the kinase is far from saturated by substrate. Neither the enzyme concentration nor a CTD Km is given, so saturation cannot be decided from the note. If all unmodified repeats bind alike, saturation would only reparameterise time by a factor common to every reaction (the same sequence of distributions, a different clock). With three post-zero time points that clock change is largely absorbed by kmod and cp, so it is named unresolved rather than built in. With cp = 1 and q_proc = 0 the count distribution is binomial(8, 1 - exp(-r*t)): the independent-repeat ('nothing at all') hypothesis.

full rationale
ATP is a required entity, and the note states one ATP per phosphorylation. At most 800 uM of the 3000 uM is consumed, so with any K_ATP in the tens of uM the factor stays near 0.98 throughout. ATP is saturating, and its depletion cannot shape the data. K_ATP is therefore fixed, not estimated: no part of the data window constrains it. Mass action in ATP was rejected because it would impose a ~27% rate decline by 16 h as an artefact of the rate-law form.

Five candidates. M1 is the base: independent repeats, strictly distributive. M2 switches on count cooperativity (cp estimated). M3 adds the nearest-neighbour effect (positional patch, nb estimated). M4 switches on processivity (q_proc estimated). M5 combines the neighbour effect with count cooperativity (nb and cp estimated) and says so.
The intent asks for a three-way test (neighbour effect, count cooperativity, nothing at all) and a check of the distributive-versus-processive conclusion. …
full rationale
The intent asks for a three-way test (neighbour effect, count cooperativity, nothing at all) and a check of the distributive-versus-processive conclusion. M1 is the 'nothing at all' and distributive reference that every 'required' verdict is measured against. M2, M3 and M4 each switch on exactly one feature. M5 is the model that contains M2 and M3 as nested cases, so the comparisons 'neighbour effect beyond count cooperativity' and the converse are direct, and the joint nb-cp profile is where the separability question is answered. Every switch acts on its own: cp, nb and q_proc each change the dynamics with the others at their neutral values. No candidate differs from another only in an inert switch.

The neighbour effect, which the base cannot express, is added as a patch in M3 and M5. The patch implements construction's positional rule exactly: rate per unmodified repeat = kmod*PTEFb*ATP/(K_ATP + ATP)*cp^n*nb^m, with m the number of marked immediate neighbours. It is written out state by state and reaction by reaction on 74 gap-structure classes and 257 reactions. These are the exact lumping of the 256-configuration, 1024-reaction model.
An unmodified repeat's rate depends only on n and on whether its two neighbours are marked. …
full rationale
An unmodified repeat's rate depends only on n and on whether its two neighbours are marked. That is fixed by its position inside the maximal stretch of unmarked repeats (gap) that contains it, and by the gap's type: interior (marks on both sides), end (chain terminus on one side), or the whole unmodified chain. Modifying a repeat changes only its own gap: it splits the gap into at most two gaps of determined types, or shrinks it by one. The multiset of gap lengths with their types is therefore a sufficient state. The lengths of marked runs, the order of interior gaps and the orientation of the chain do not enter any rate; the rule treats both termini alike. Configurations sharing a gap structure have identical exit rates to every target class, so the 256 configurations are strongly lumpable onto the 74 classes. The classes with n marks sum to the count distribution exactly, at every nb and cp. Built-in check: at nb = 1 every class with n marks has total exit coefficient 8 - n (for example G01_22: 5*nb), so M3 reproduces M1 and M5 reproduces M2 trajectory for trajectory. Writing the reduced network by hand carries far less risk of an enumeration error than 1024 hand-written lines.

In M3 and M5 the class reactions carry the count bookkeeping. Each G reaction from a class with n marks also converts CTD_n + ATP -> CTD_n+1 + ADP, at the same rate. J0 to J7 are kept, with their stoichiometry, at zero rate. The observation model is unchanged: phos<n>_rel maps onto CTD_n.
This keeps CTD_n as the readout species shared by all five candidates, and it keeps ATP consumed exactly once per modification. …
full rationale
This keeps CTD_n as the readout species shared by all five candidates, and it keeps ATP consumed exactly once per modification. Every flux into or out of a class with n marks moves CTD_n by the same amount, and CTD_n(0) equals its class sum, so CTD_n equals the sum of its classes identically. That identity now holds by stoichiometry, not by matching summed coefficients, so an error in any one coefficient cannot break it. A linear multistep integrator preserves the linear invariant to solver precision. The class reactions are the base's distributive single-repeat steps resolved by position, so J0 to J7 at zero rate are superseded, not contradicted. The base's processive Jp* reactions likewise sit at exactly zero rate in M3 and M5, where q_proc stays 0 and processivity is not composed with the positional model. The class rate laws read only the class amount, so listing CTD_n as a reactant changes no rate. The deliberate simplification is a second conservation class (sum over G = 100 uM) alongside sum over CTD_n = 100 uM. Both are intended and neither carries a free parameter.

all alternatives considered
The previous structure, in which the J0 to J7 rates were rewritten as the summed class fluxes. It is mathematically equivalent, but the engine's symbol check refused it twice: a replacement line may not use species declared in another patch (attempts 1 and 2). Assignment rules CTD_n := sum of G_n were also rejected. They would require removing CTD_n from all 36 base reactions, which the patch grammar does not allow.

Revision on human feedback and the gate errors. In M3_neighbour and M5_neighbour_and_count, adds_parameters holds only nb, as asked. The 74 gap classes (Gf8, G07 ... G00) are declared as species, with their initial amounts, in each candidate's append block; they are not parameters. The engine refused that same layout because the J0 to J7 replacement lines used G species that neither the base nor adds_parameters declares. Those replacement lines therefore no longer reference any G species: J0 to J7 are set to zero rate, and each class reaction in the append carries the CTD_n + ATP -> CTD_n+1 + ADP conversion. Everything else is unchanged: candidate ids, set_parameters, the values and bounds of nb, cp and q_proc, every class reaction's rate expression, every class species and its initial amount, and every glossary entry.

full rationale
I could not satisfy 'change nothing else' and pass the gate at the same time. The previous reply already did exactly what was asked, and the gate refused M3 and M5 for the reason it gave in attempt 1. A replace_reaction line may use only symbols from the base or adds_parameters, and putting the classes in adds_parameters is what petablint rejected. The closest defensible change touches only the lines the gate names (the eight J replacements) and moves their job, moving CTD_n and consuming ATP, into the class reactions. The model is the same: every species trajectory, and therefore the likelihood, matches the previous structure, because CTD_n equals the class sum in both. The gate never flagged the append block, even though it uses every G symbol. That suggests each patch is checked against its own declarations plus the base and adds_parameters, and not against other patches. The replacement lines now use base symbols only, so they pass under either reading.
general_knowledge [human_feedback: petablint rejected the G species as extraneous parameters in the parameter table; keep only nb in adds_parameters] — the classes stay out of adds_parametersgeneral_knowledge [previous_attempt_errors and attempt_history (attempts 1 and 2): only the eight J replacement patches flagged, never the append] — the gate checks replacement lines against the base and adds_parameters only; the append's own declarations are accepted
alternatives: Reordering the patches so the append comes first. Not chosen: the append's acceptance suggests the check is per patch, not cumulative, so the order would probably not matter. …
all alternatives considered
Reordering the patches so the append comes first. Not chosen: the append's acceptance suggests the check is per patch, not cumulative, so the order would probably not matter. Putting the classes back in adds_parameters: rejected, because petablint refuses them. Changing the engine's symbol check to accept species declared in another patch of the same candidate: that would let the previous structure stand and is the engine maintainers' call, but this reply does not depend on it.
